module

public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.Digraph.Basic
public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.Digraph.Orientation
public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic
public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite
public import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Card
public import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic

@[expose] public section

namespace Digraph

variable {V W : Type*}

/--
A **tournament** is a directed graph in which every pair of distinct vertices is connected
by exactly one directed edge.
-/
def IsTournament (G : Digraph V) : Prop :=
  (∀ v, ¬ G.Adj v v) ∧ (∀ u v, u ≠ v → (G.Adj u v ↔ ¬ G.Adj v u))

/--
An **orientation** of an undirected simple graph `H` is a digraph `D` whose edges
are obtained by directing each edge of `H` in exactly one direction.
-/
def IsOrientation (D : Digraph V) (H : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  (∀ u v, D.Adj u v → H.Adj u v) ∧ (∀ u v, H.Adj u v → (D.Adj u v ↔ ¬ D.Adj v u))

variable [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Fintype W] [DecidableEq W]

/--
The type of digraph homomorphisms `D →g D'`.
A function `f : V → W` is a digraph homomorphism if `D.Adj u v → D'.Adj (f u) (f v)`.
Note that `f` is a general mapping and is not required to be injective.
-/
structure Hom (D : Digraph V) (D' : Digraph W) where
  toFun : V → W
  map_adj' : ∀ {u v : V}, D.Adj u v → D'.Adj (toFun u) (toFun v)

infixl:50 " →g " => Digraph.Hom

instance (D : Digraph V) (D' : Digraph W) : CoeFun (D →g D') (fun _ => V → W) :=
  ⟨Digraph.Hom.toFun⟩

noncomputable instance (D : Digraph V) (D' : Digraph W) [DecidableRel D.Adj] [DecidableRel D'.Adj] :
    Fintype (D →g D') :=
  Fintype.ofInjective (fun f => f.toFun) (fun f g h => by cases f; cases g; congr)

/--
The number of homomorphisms from a digraph `D` to a digraph `D'`.
-/
noncomputable def homCount (D : Digraph V) (D' : Digraph W) [DecidableRel D.Adj] [DecidableRel D'.Adj] : ℕ :=
  Fintype.card (D →g D')

/--
The **homomorphism density** $t_D(D')$ of a digraph $D$ in a digraph $D'$.
It is defined as `#Hom(D, D') / |W|^{|V|}`.
-/
noncomputable def homDensity (D : Digraph V) (D' : Digraph W)
    [DecidableRel D.Adj] [DecidableRel D'.Adj] : ℝ :=
  (homCount D D' : ℝ) / (Fintype.card W : ℝ) ^ (Fintype.card V)

end Digraph

findings.description: In the consuming file FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/SidorenkoConjecture.lean:188–213, the hypothesis uses a local predicate `IsSpider234` that does not characterize the (2,3,4)-spider. It requires three selected leaves at distances 2, 3, and 4 from a degree-three vertex, but neither requires these to be all the leaves nor excludes additional branching. A Lean-certified counterexample has vertices 0,…,9 and undirected edges {01,02,03,14,15,56,27,78,89}. It satisfies `IsSpider234` with center 0 and selected leaves 4,6,9. However, it has four leaves (3,4,6,9) and two degree-three vertices (0,1), so it is not a three-legged spider. Thus the predicate used by this problem has the wrong meaning. This is a consumer-local defect, not an error in `Digraph.IsOrientation`, `IsTournament`, or `homDensity`; it does not establish that the enlarged TAS assertion is false.
findings.source_evidence: Chen–Clemen–Noel, On Tournament Anti-Sidorenko Orientations of Trees, https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14138, §1 (LaTeX source, paragraph defining spiders and theorem labelled `th:3spider`): an (a₁,…,aₖ)-spider is obtained from disjoint paths of those lengths by identifying one endpoint of each; every 3-spider admits a TAS orientation. The original problem is He–Mani–Nie–Tung–Wei, https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.11222, Problem 1.6: “Find a TAS orientation of the 2-3-4 tree.” Such a tree has exactly three leaves and one degree-three vertex.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct `SidorenkoConjecture.IsSpider234`, preferably by requiring isomorphism to an explicit (2,3,4)-spider. Alternatively, retain the existing conditions and add `∀ v, v ≠ center → v ≠ l₁ → v ≠ l₂ → v ≠ l₃ → T.degree v = 2`. With the tree hypothesis and prescribed degrees/distances, this forces precisely the three intended legs.

findings.description: The new structure at Tournament.lean:52–54 duplicates the existing Mathlib type `RelHom D.Adj D'.Adj`: both consist of an underlying function and exactly the same adjacency-preservation proof. Mathlib also already provides its function coercion and the corresponding Fintype instance. The mathematics is correct; this is only duplication of existing library machinery. An explicit equivalence between the two types was proved in the scratch file.
findings.source_evidence: Mathlib/Order/RelIso/Basic.lean:46–50 defines `RelHom` with fields `toFun` and `map_rel'`. Mathlib/Data/Fintype/Pi.lean:154–158 supplies `RelHom.instFintype` under the same finite-type and decidable-relation assumptions. Mathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Maps.lean:292–293 already uses `abbrev Hom := RelHom G.Adj G'.Adj` for the analogous graph notion.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `abbrev Hom (D : Digraph V) (D' : Digraph W) := RelHom D.Adj D'.Adj`, retain the graph notation, and reuse Mathlib's coercion and Fintype instance instead of recreating them.

reformulations.difference: The definition uses `G.Adj u v ↔ ¬ G.Adj v u` for distinct vertices rather than explicitly saying exactly one direction exists or that G is an orientation of the complete simple graph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Classically, `P ↔ ¬Q` is equivalent to `(P ∨ Q) ∧ ¬(P ∧ Q)`. Together with the explicit prohibition of self-loops, this is precisely a tournament. Both the exclusive-direction characterization and `G.IsTournament ↔ G.IsOrientation (SimpleGraph.completeGraph V)` were proved for arbitrary vertex types in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: Looplessness and equality of the underlying undirected graph are not separate fields; the definition instead uses an adjacency-subset condition and a biconditional on each edge of H.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The subset condition excludes loops because H is a SimpleGraph. On every edge of H, the biconditional forces one and only one direction. Conversely, an asymmetric digraph whose underlying inclusive simple graph is H satisfies these two clauses. The equivalence with `(∀ u v, D.Adj u v → ¬ D.Adj v u) ∧ D.toSimpleGraphInclusive = H` was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: This variant quantifies over tournamentons rather than the finite tournaments in the original TAS trees conjecture.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each fixed orientation D, the finite-tournament upper bound passes to tournamentons by finite sampling/approximation and convergence of homomorphism densities, as discussed explicitly in §1 of arXiv:2512.11222. Conversely, represent a finite tournament by an equal-part step tournamenton, putting 1/2 on same-part blocks. Its D-density is at least the finite tournament's D-density, since this only adds nonnegative contributions to the adjacency-product formula. Therefore the tournamenton upper bound implies the finite bound. This holds for each D, so the existential orientation quantifier is preserved.

review.notes: All five named definitions, both instances, and the notation in Tournament.lean were checked. Apart from the minor RelHom duplication, their mathematical meanings agree with the standard notions. The consumer's spider predicate is the only mathematical mismatch found. Lean tests in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/spider.lean compile without errors or warnings. Tests cover empty and singleton vertex types, loops, antiparallel arcs, cyclic tournaments, noninjective homomorphisms, enumeration/count agreement, and density normalization. In particular, an empty source has density 1 even in an empty host, while a nonempty source in an empty host has density 0; every finite-tournament consumer assumes a nonempty host, so this totalized division causes no use-site defect. The spider counterexample proof depends only on Lean's standard axioms, not on any sorry-backed problem theorem. No repository source files were changed.

not_fixed.reason: The defect is in `SidorenkoConjecture.IsSpider234`, defined in FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/SidorenkoConjecture.lean, which is outside the permitted editing scope. There is no valid in-file portion of this fix in Tournament.lean. The consumer predicate needs an additional condition requiring every vertex other than the center and the three selected leaves to have degree 2, or replacement by isomorphism to an explicit (2,3,4)-spider. Changing the correct tournament-library definitions would not be a legitimate repair.

submission.summary: No files were edited. Confirmed that Tournament.lean still matches its committed content and that the required Lean compile command reports no errors or warnings. The reported defect cannot be corrected within the sole permitted file.
